campaign.title: Small-angle collapse of the subcritical angular symbol

resource_policy.literature_policy: Use internal exact profile and recombination theorems. Search primary literature only if a one-sided character-divisor radial theorem is proposed.

frozen_target.question: For n asymp X^nu with 0<nu<1/2, does the exact floor-perturbed angular multiplier collapse to the hard one-sided divisor cone with O(n/sqrt X) error, and over what range is that error target-safe?
frozen_target.candidate_error: sum_(n asymp N)n^(-3/4)tau(n)n/sqrt X << N^(5/4+epsilon)/sqrt X, target-safe at fixed nu<2/5.

completion_criteria: Prove or refute the exact angular multiplier collapse with all floors, stars, top, and bottom owners.
Audit the Taylor bound Phi(u)-1=O(u^2) uniformly on every supported active scale.
Derive the sharp total radial error and exact threshold, including endpoint logarithms.
Identify the limiting one-sided character-divisor coefficient exactly.
Attempt a signed bound or prove an exact return/capacity obstruction for the limiting radial sum.
A clean statement-only rederivation and an independent hostile/source audit exist.
No downstream exponent promotion occurs without a new signed estimate.

tasks.target: Prove the strongest exact small-angle collapse and error range, then attack the resulting one-sided character-divisor radial sum.
Using only the Round-62 packet, independently prove or refute the multiplier identity, total error, and two-fifths threshold.

Hostilely test floors, active support, telescope/stars, bottom ownership, the N^(5/4)/sqrt X ledger, and whether any known primary theorem estimates the resulting one-sided character-divisor radial sum.

review_seams.requirement: The floor, top, bottom, and star conventions must give one exact limiting coefficient, not a schematic partition.
The O(n/sqrt X) pointwise symbol error and its N^(5/4)/sqrt X radial sum must be proved with divisor multiplicity and endpoint logs.
Any simplification or estimate for the one-sided divisor coefficient must retain chi_4 and the angular cutoff.
A target-safe replacement error does not bound the limiting signed radial sum or improve the Gauss exponent.
